scope: Splendor core game, 1st edition (2014), complete authoritative extracted/splendor-rules.txt. No expansions or later-edition additions.

questions.question: You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?

You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?

A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?

A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?

You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?

You have no tokens, no purchased developments and no reserved cards. A face-up level-3 development is far too expensive for you to buy. May you reserve it anyway? Do you pay its printed cost when reserving, and do you take gold if available?

Instead of reserving a face-up card, you reserve the top card of the level-2 deck while twelve face-up market cards remain. Must any market card be removed or refilled because of that blind reservation, how many market cards remain, and can you take a second card as a replacement in your hand?

A level deck has run out, but its four face-up cards are still in the market. Must those cards be removed, or may they still be purchased or reserved? If one is purchased, what happens to that space and to the other three cards?

All development decks and face-up market cards have been exhausted; nobody has reached fifteen prestige. A player still has an affordable reserved card and gems are available in at least three colors. Does exhaustion itself end the game? May that player buy the reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action?

You already own ten tokens. Three different gem colors are available. Can you take one of each and then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with exactly the same token holdings? Is a net gain of tokens required?

The gold supply is empty. On A’s turn, A pays two gold while purchasing a card. B then reserves a card with fewer than three cards reserved. Are A’s spent gold tokens removed from the game, or can B take one, and how many gold tokens are left in the supply immediately after B’s reservation before any token-limit returns?
You have bought no level-1 or level-2 developments, but can pay for a face-up level-3 card. May you purchase that level-3 card now, or must you unlock its level by buying lower-level cards first?

You have twelve prestige, then purchase a three-prestige development whose bonus also makes you qualify for a noble. May you stop at fifteen and skip the noble visit? What is your total after your turn, and can the other players who still have a turn in the round continue playing?

Four players act A, B, C, D, with A first. D is the first player to reach fifteen prestige on D’s turn. Does A start another round, does everyone get one more turn, or is the game over after D completes this turn? Explain using equal turn counts.

In a two-player game, three nobles were revealed and the other seven removed during setup. After someone receives one noble, do you reveal a new tile from those seven to restore the display to three? Where does the acquired tile go and how many nobles remain available in the middle?
Match each component name to its color: emerald, diamond, sapphire, onyx, ruby and gold joker. How many development cards are in the box in total and at each of the three levels?
